system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current
T6: Attributing Debezium/CDC when portfolio and notes are omitted (CV does not mention it)

# OUTPUT 1: CV
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience building and operating batch and streaming data
platforms for e-commerce, payments and logistics. Experienced in owning data platform ingestion,
developing reusable pipelines with Airflow and dbt, and improving data quality through testing and
data contracts. Built production systems processing approximately 30 million events per day and 1.2
TB of raw files daily.
SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data platforms and engineering: Airflow, dbt, PySpark, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Redshift,
PostgreSQL, Great Expectations
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub
Actions
Data and BI: Dimensional modelling, data quality, data contracts, Power BI, Looker (basic)
EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace) | 03/2022 -
Present
• Own the ingestion layer of the company data platform, maintaining approximately 140 Airflow
DAGs that load from Postgres, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake.
• Migrated transformation logic from stored procedures to dbt, building 420+ models with tests on
every model; reduced nightly run time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes.
• Introduced JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product teams and the data team,
reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately 9 per month to 2 per month.
• Built a Kafka-based event pipeline using Kafka Connect and Snowpipe Streaming for shipment
tracking, processing approximately 30 million events per day.
• Mentor two mid-level data engineers and run weekly data platform office hours.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay (payments startup) | 09/2019 - 02/2022
• Built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR for transaction reconciliation, processing approximately 1.2 TB
of raw files from S3 daily.
• Designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse schema with 30+ fact and dimension tables for finance
and risk teams.
• Implemented Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables.
• Developed an internal Python library for S3 and Glue catalog access, adopted by four teams.
Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group | 06/2017 - 08/2019
• Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL processes for an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
• Built Power BI reports for store operations across 40+ stores.
• Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.
EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role at Halden Pay. Over nine
years in data engineering, I have built and operated batch and streaming platforms across
logistics, payments and retail, with a focus on dependable pipelines, clear data contracts and
data that downstream teams can trust.
In my current role, I own the ingestion layer of a data platform spanning approximately 140
Airflow DAGs and sources including Postgres, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs, with
data loaded into Snowflake. I moved transformation logic to dbt, building more than 420
tested models and reducing the nightly run from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I
also introduced JSON Schema contracts with CI checks, which reduced broken-pipeline
incidents from approximately nine per month to two. These experiences align closely with
your focus on owning a shared platform, building reusable frameworks and defining data
quality standards.
I have also worked with large-scale event and cloud data workloads: a Kafka-based shipment
tracking pipeline processing approximately 30 million events per day, and PySpark
reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files daily. My
warehouse experience includes designing a Redshift dimensional schema with more than 30
fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams. Across these roles, I have worked to turn
the needs of product, finance and risk colleagues into reliable data capabilities, and I bring
hands-on experience with Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Docker and CI checks.
Halden Pay’s emphasis on a shared Data Platform team and reusable solutions is a strong fit
for the platform work I have led. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
experience in platform ownership, data modelling and operational data quality could
contribute to the team.
Sincerely, Lena Varga-Holm

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
